area: A fresh claim inherits the predecessor's work-admission ticket grant, which then silently narrows commit authority below the claim it is bound to
finding: Commit authority is the intersection of the active claim's file list and the work-admission ticket's file-write grant: a non-empty grant filters the claim rather than describing it. When a task changes hands, the newly minted claim can carry a ticket whose grant still holds the predecessor's file set while its claimGeneration correctly matches the new lease. The ticket therefore looks internally consistent under every identity check — right task, right actor, right lease — yet authorizes a different body of work than the claim it belongs to. The consequence is silent and misleading rather than fail-closed: paths that sit squarely inside the live claim are reported to the operator as external dirty files, in the same list as unrelated repository noise. Nothing in the output names the ticket, the grant, or the intersection, so the observed symptom points at scope while the cause lives one layer away. An operator debugging this will re-check scope, re-read the direction lock, and find them correct, because they are.
expectedBehavior: A ticket's grant must be derived from the claim it is bound to, at the moment that claim is created, so a grant can never describe a different generation of work than its claimGeneration asserts. Where the two can still diverge, the divergence must be detected rather than applied: a grant narrower than its own active claim is an internally inconsistent authority record and should fail closed with a diagnostic that names both sets, not silently reclassify in-claim paths as foreign. State it as the general rule — when two authority records intersect to produce a decision, a refusal must identify which record excluded the path, because the operator cannot otherwise tell which one to repair.
evidenceOrRepro: 2026-08-16, ATM-GOV-0369 after an official handoff from cursor-captain to claude-008. The new claim's files listed 28 paths including the four backlog documents and the card's source files. The task's workAdmissionTicket carried claimGeneration lease-ddd621457884, matching the new claim exactly, but its file-write grant held only the 11 paths of the predecessor's publication bundle (.atm evidence for 0369, packages/cli/dist, release/atm-onefile, release/atm-root-drop). `git commit --auto-stage --dry-run` resolved a bundle containing only ledger and task-event files and listed all four in-claim backlog documents under skippedExternalDirtyFiles, alongside genuinely unrelated dirty files, with no mention of the ticket. Isolating the cause required reading commit-authority-scopes.ts, where a non-empty ticketScopes acts as an intersecting filter over an already-matched claim scope. Running the official `tasks scope add` with the same four paths returned ATM_SCOPE_AMENDMENT_APPLIED with addedPaths [] — every path was already present — while the ticket's file-write grant went from 11 entries to 28. No scope changed; only the stale ticket was re-minted, which isolates the ticket as the sole blocking factor. The bundle then resolved correctly.
followUp: Decide where the grant is authored and make that the only place it can be authored, then cover the handoff and takeover transitions specifically, since those are the transitions where a claim is replaced while its ticket is not. Do not repair this by widening the intersection or by treating an empty grant as permissive; the intersection is the correct shape and the defect is that one side of it went stale. Related to [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-003], which records a different way the work-admission ticket gate obscures the specific blocker underneath it — together they suggest the ticket layer needs to explain itself in refusals generally, not only in this transition.
